subject: Request: Temporary SLA amendment for uptime & p95 latency during onboarding spike
messages:
From: Aiden Clarke <aiden.clarke@horizonai.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary SLA amendment request for onboarding surge

Hi Diego —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Quick ask from our side: Horizon is about to onboard a major partner (3x expected peak), and our infra team is concerned about hitting the standard SLA thresholds during the first 90 days. Specifically we expect a high-volume ramp that could temporarily push p95 latency above our usual tolerances and cause a few short regional availability blips during mass syncs.

Would Redwood consider a short-term amendment to the hosted SLA for HZN-4571 that: 
- Temporarily adjusts uptime baseline from 99.9% to 99.5% for a 90-day pilot window,
- Provides a capped monthly service credit formula for that window, and
- Adds an explicit maintenance/fallback carveout for bulk syncs (we propose a 4-hour rolling carveout per week during the pilot).

We can share traffic projections (attached) and are open to a phased approach (gradual return to baseline as traffic normalizes). Procurement is hoping to finalize terms by next Friday — can we discuss options this week?

Attachments: HorizonAI-traffic-projections.xlsx (summary + hourly ramp model)

Best,
Aiden Clarke
Head of Cloud Partnerships
HorizonAI

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Aiden Clarke <aiden.clarke@horizonai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 18:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA amendment request for onboarding surge

Aiden — thanks for the heads up and for the projection file. I’ve looped in Marissa (CS) and Ben (Sales/procurement) so we can evaluate operational impact and commercial terms quickly.

High-level thoughts: we’re open to a timeboxed amendment for ramp/pilot scenarios but need three things from you before we put a formal draft in front of Procurement: 
1) Confirmation of expected 95th-percentile latency during peak hours (per-region, if possible) so our SREs can size KV cache and batching parameters;
2) Concrete windows and dates for the 90-day pilot (start/end) and any planned bulk-sync windows; and
3) A single point of contact on the Horizon infra team for rapid incident triage during the pilot.

Operationally, a 99.5% provisional floor for 90 days is something we can scope — we usually prefer a phased rollback (e.g., 99.7% after 30 days, 99.8% after 60, back to 99.9% at 90) tied to measured latency improvements. For credits, we can draft a capped monthly credit formula (flat percentage of monthly invoice for each 0.1% below threshold, with an upper cap). Ben — can you draft the commercial mechanics and a short amendment template? Marissa — can you confirm support/monitoring SLA and on-call coverage expectations?

I’ll flag this as high priority. If you can send the per-region latency projection and preferred pilot dates by end of day tomorrow we’ll aim to circulate a draft amendment within 48 business hours.

Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA amendment request for onboarding surge

Aiden / team —

Thanks for the projection, Diego. I put together a short commercial frame and attached a draft amendment for review; key points below:

- Pilot window: 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-29 (90 days) — flexible if you need an earlier start.
- Uptime floor (hosted): 99.5% for month 1; automatic uplift to 99.7% in month 2 and 99.85% in month 3, reverting to standard 99.9% after closeout unless we agree otherwise.
- Latency: we won’t change the latency SLO language, but we’ll add a targeted p95 relief carveout tied to the bulk-sync windows you nominate; SREs will maintain best-effort mitigations.
- Credits: monthly credit = min( (monthly_invoice * 0.02) * ((99.5 - reported_uptime)/0.1), monthly_invoice * 0.15 ) — this caps at 15% of monthly charges for any given month during the pilot.
- Maintenance carveouts: up to 4 hours/week scheduled carveout for bulk syncs; any unscheduled regional failovers to be evaluated case-by-case.
- Termination: both parties may terminate the pilot with 14 days’ written notice; credits are pro-rated.

I attached SLA-Amendment-draft-v1.pdf (wording + redlines). Marissa, can you confirm we can provide the extra operational monitoring and a weekly sync during the pilot? Aiden, if these terms look directionally OK I can route the draft to Proc and Legal for a quick redline.

Attachments: SLA-Amendment-draft-v1.pdf

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
